decisions.decision: Before a writable rollback to 1.4.0, operators must copy the current data file so reactivation can recover previously assigned deadlines by ticket ID while keeping changes made during the rollback.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted deadline storage that survives 1.4.0 writes and supports reactivation without a separate operator-managed copy.

decisions.decision: Backfill uses the priority currently stored on each ticket, even if it changed after creation.
decisions.alternative: They might have meant to use the ticket's original priority, recovered from its creation audit entry where available.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:17 (R-3); record/03-research.md:17 (stored priority for legacy rows)

decisions.decision: Backfill uses the response-hour settings in effect when it assigns a missing deadline.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted legacy tickets backfilled with the initially specified hours and overrides applied only to new tickets.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9 (R-1 settings) and :17 (R-3 backfill and changed settings)

decisions.decision: With DUE_TIMES=on, an existing file with missing deadlines causes the entire service to fail before it starts listening.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the service to keep answering with due times disabled and to report that activation was blocked until operators fixed the file.

decisions.decision: An enabled service may start empty when the configured data file is absent or when it runs in memory.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted enabled startup to require a prepared data file unless the operator explicitly authorizes an empty start.

decisions.decision: The specification assigns deadlines on the enabled ticket-creation path and leaves tickets created while disabled to receive deadlines through backfill.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted deadlines recorded at creation even while disabled, with the flag controlling only whether the API shows and filters by them.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9 (R-1 enabled creation), :17 (R-3 missing deadlines), and :21 (R-4 disabled writes)

decisions.decision: Invalid response-hour settings cause a clear failure when due times are active.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the service to warn about invalid settings and continue using the documented hours for the affected priorities.

decisions.decision: Backfill replaces the data file atomically and leaves the original file intact if the run fails.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted backfill to save completed batches so operators could resume from a partial migration after a failure.

decisions.decision: The overdue filter requires an active, past-due ticket and keeps the existing rule that a ticket can match either status or priority when both filters are supplied.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted an overdue search with both filters to require a match on both status and priority, as the API documentation describes for combined filters.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:13 (R-2 existing filter behavior); record/02-discovery.md:25 (existing OR behavior); repo/docs/api.md:76 (documented filter behavior)

decisions.decision: Overdue results use the existing ticket-ID order and cursor pagination.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the earliest deadlines first so operators could work from the most overdue tickets.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:13 (R-2 cursor behavior); repo/docs/api.md:79 (existing order and pagination)

decisions.decision: Backfill adds deadlines while leaving the existing audit history in place without recording a deadline assignment for each ticket.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted each backfilled deadline recorded in the ticket history so operators could trace when it was assigned.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:17 (R-3 audit preservation) and :29 (R-6 audit compatibility)

decisions.decision: The raw CLI output keeps the existing column positions when due times are enabled.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted a due column next to priority and been willing to update the weekly report and other positional consumers.

decisions.decision: The human-readable CLI shows a deadline only when DUE_TIMES is on and the file contains the value.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the CLI to show stored deadlines before activation so operators could inspect the backfill with the flag still off.
